title: Isochronous tile: throughput vs latency comparison - Oct 2029 (draft)
content:
Purpose
------
Quick exploratory benchmark comparing two insertion/packing strategies we refer to internally as:
- isochronous-tiling (iso-tile): fixed-time-slot allocation, deterministic slot placement, trade higher idle over lower jitter
- opportunistic-tiling (op-tile): dynamic packing that fills slots opportunistically for throughput

Goal: characterize latency tail (p50/p90/p99), steady throughput (qps), and cost per 1k tokens for a representative chat workload (avg turn 60 tokens, 1–6 turns/session). This is an internal draft: notes, ASCII charts, and action items.

Environment & methodology
-------------------------
- Cluster: staging-dedicated-gpu-48 (8xA100-80GB nodes)
- Runtime build: inference-runtime@main (PR 4123) with tile-packing toggles exposed
- Workload generator: local harness that replays recorded production traces (sampled 2029-09) scaled to target QPS
- Key knobs: tile_duration_ms = {5,10,20}, max_slots_per_gpu = {32,64}, prefetch=false
- Measurements: p50/p90/p99 latency (ms) for generation request, median tokens/s per GPU, cost estimate (dollars per 1k tokens) using our internal instance-cost model
- Each data point is median of 5 runs; runs lasted 12 minutes after a 3-minute warmup

Test matrix (short)
-------------------
We tested iso-tile vs op-tile across three target sustained QPS levels: 50, 200, 800. All runs used model xlarge-8 (quantized) to keep cost comparable.

ASCII summary table (median of runs)
-----------------------------------
Config                 | QPS tgt | achieved QPS | p50(ms) | p90(ms) | p99(ms) | tokens/1k cost($)
-----------------------+---------+--------------+---------+---------+---------+------------------
iso-tile (5ms)         | 50      | 48           | 42      | 65      | 180     | 0.042            
iso-tile (10ms)        | 200     | 196          | 55      | 89      | 260     | 0.036            
iso-tile (20ms)        | 800     | 770          | 120     | 230     | 540     | 0.031            
op-tile (optimize)     | 50      | 50           | 36      | 60      | 150     | 0.045            
op-tile (optimize)     | 200     | 205          | 70      | 140     | 420     | 0.028            
op-tile (aggressive)   | 800     | 830          | 190     | 410     | 980     | 0.025            

Quick takeaways
---------------
- Small QPS (50): op-tile gives slightly lower latency across the board (p50/p90/p99), but cost per token is ~7% higher due to less predictable packing and more idle prefills on our cost model.
- Mid QPS (200): iso-tile (10ms) balances lower p90 and acceptable p99; op-tile pushes higher throughput but shows larger p90/p99 variance (indicative of contention-triggered stalls).
- High QPS (800): iso-tile with larger tile_duration (20ms) yields better p99 than op-tile aggressive packing but at the expense of higher median latency. Op-tile can hit slightly higher sustained QPS but p99 degrades substantially.

Interpretation notes
--------------------
- Iso-tile appears to act as a shock absorber: deterministic slot boundaries help bound tail latency when internal preemption/eviction occurs. The cost-per-1k tokens improves at scale (amortization), which is why iso-tile 20ms shows lower cost though higher median latency.
- Op-tile is more efficient peak-to-peak (higher achieved QPS in aggressive mode) but sensitive to session mix: bursts of long-turn users cause carries that cascade into p99 spikes.
- These results map to the thesis: if customer SLOs prioritize predictable p99 (e.g., interactive applications), iso-tile with tuned tile_duration is preferable; if throughput/cost is primary (batch embedding or asynchronous jobs), op-tile may win.

Text charts (sparkline-like, relative)
------------------------------------
Latency tail trend (lower is better):
50 QPS: iso: ▅▅▆▇▇ | op: ▅▅▅▆▇
200 QPS: iso: ▅▆▇▇▇ | op: ▅▇▇▇▇
800 QPS: iso: ▆▇▇▇▇ | op: ▇▇▇▇▇

Cost vs p99 (qualitative):
- iso-5ms: cost ↑ slightly, p99 moderate
- iso-20ms: cost ↓ at scale, p99 improved vs op-tile
- op-tile aggressive: cost lowest, p99 worst (high variance)

Open questions / follow-ups
--------------------------
- Does iso-tile behavior change materially with prefetch=true? we disabled prefetch in this run; need a follow-up matrix.
- Interaction with KV cache hit rate: our trace sample has ~35% KV hit; run a 70% hit trace to see how amortization shifts.
- Multi-tenant interference: these runs are single-tenant; schedule a small run with a noisy co-tenant to measure fragility.
- Cost model sanity check: tokens/1k cost based on our internal price list; reconcile with finance if using spot-backed nodes (dedicated reserved vs hoster).

Recommendations (actionable)
---------------------------
1) Short-term: for the next canary release, enable iso-tile default for interactive product routes (chat) with tile_duration_ms=10; provide a toggle in the console to drop to op-tile for cost-focused routes. (Owner: Marco)
2) Medium-term: rerun systematic matrix with prefetch=true and high-KV-hit trace; add multi-tenant simulation. (Owner: Lina)
3) Product: add a console metric that surfaces slot-utilization percent and per-route pack-variance (Owner: Samir).

Notes to self / rough log
------------------------
- Run artifacts: dash urls above contain per-run traces + qtrace logs. Will export pcap for the 800 QPS iso-20ms run.
- Observed periodic 1–2s stalls at ~t=7:30 in several op-tile runs; need to correlate with GC and kernel preemption logs.
- Consider running smaller model (xlarge-4) to validate cost curves across model sizes.

Appendix: sample raw run snippet (p99 series)
-------------------------------------------
- iso-tile 20ms / 800 tgt: p99 series across 5 runs = [540, 520, 560, 530, 550] ms (std ~14ms)
- op-tile aggressive / 800 tgt: p99 series = [980, 720, 1120, 860, 1000] ms (std ~160ms)

Unresolved wording for final brief
--------------------------------
- предпочитаемая терминология: "isochronous tile" vs "fixed-tile"? engineering prefers iso-tile shorthand; product docs may want the longer phrase.
- Should we expose tile_duration as "latency-smoothing-window" in console? UX asked for consumer-friendly naming.

End of draft.
